name: design-doc
description: Run an assumptions-first architecture design — registers with stable IDs (A#/DQ#/V#), decision-by-question rounds with a recorded escape hatch, a mid-process adversarial review, a library of quantitative components (request paths, load ceilings, number tables) whose estimates are gated on named spikes — and ship the result as an interactive HTML doc that opens on a full-screen summary deck of 3–5 panels (or one poster), draws its system diagram with Mermaid behind a ten-node overview, cites every entry by a human-readable handle, twins every register entry with a plain-English version the reader sees first, carries declared interactive components (what-if, steps, timeline, matrix, and the self-laying-out compare figures flow and lanes) plus compiled TSX as the escape hatch, links every decision and open item to the pull requests that land it with live GitHub state behind a deployed token, replays the interview round by round, and, behind a deployed key, answers questions from the whole document and moves the page from an Ask bar that stays collapsed at the bottom right until it docks into an assistant panel, and from a Cmd-K palette that answers inline, plus a PDF printed from the same page, written as a humble proposal that explains and asks for feedback rather than sells.
